ca_joshua_tree_national_park.blurb: Joshua Tree sits in the high desert of southern California, near Twentynine Palms, where piles of rounded monzogranite rise out of open desert flats. It is a trad-first destination: cracks, slabs and steep faces make up most of the climbing, with a solid bouldering scene and a smaller helping of sport and top-rope lines. Grades run from easy to very hard, but the bulk sits between 5.8 and 5.11, with the heaviest concentration at 5.10, and boulder problems cluster in the lower V grades. Formations are scattered across the park rather than packed into one cliff band, so a trip means moving between zones such as Hidden Valley, Indian Cove, Queen Valley, Lost Horse and the Wonderland of Rocks. Cooler months suit the exposed rock best.

ut_wasatch_range.blurb: The Wasatch runs from northern Utah near the Idaho line down past Mount Nebo, with its canyons cut into the mountains above Ogden, Salt Lake City and Provo. The rock changes from canyon to canyon: quartzite in Big Cottonwood and around Ogden, granite-like quartz monzonite in Little Cottonwood, and pocketed limestone in American Fork and Logan. Sport climbing is the largest share, followed by bouldering and trad, with some ice, mixed and alpine routes on top. Grades span the whole ladder, though most routes fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with plenty of moderates. Shaded canyons stay workable in summer heat, higher limestone sees snow early, and winter brings ice. The Central Wasatch is the busiest part, ahead of the Southern and Northern sections.

ca_sierra_eastside.blurb: The Eastside follows the high-desert foot of the Sierra along the Owens Valley, with Bishop as the main hub and Mammoth Lakes, June Lake and Lone Pine as other bases. Bouldering and sport climbing dominate, with a healthy amount of trad and a thin layer of alpine and ice. Volcanic welded tuff forms the gorge walls and tablelands, while granite shows up in the large boulders of the foothills, the canyon cliffs and the high peaks above. Most routes land from 5.9 to 5.12, and boulder problems stretch from beginner to very hard. Lower-elevation areas near Bishop and the Alabama Hills work in cooler months, while higher valleys such as Rock Creek offer relief from summer heat.

nv_southern_nevada.blurb: Southern Nevada centres on Las Vegas, with climbing reachable within an hour or so in several directions. Red Rocks, about twenty miles west of town, holds most of the routes: red sandstone cliffs with a wide mix of sport, trad, bouldering and multi-pitch climbing, and a reputation for generous moderates. Sandstone weakens when wet, so conditions matter. Mount Charleston, in the Spring Mountains, is a cooler limestone escape with steep, often overhanging sport routes. Smaller zones such as Keyhole Canyon, Mount Potosi and the La Madre Range add other rock types. Most routes sit between 5.8 and 5.12, with a good moderate spread, and boulders run from easy to hard. Spring and fall are the favourite seasons at low elevation.

az_central_arizona.blurb: Central Arizona spreads across the low desert around Phoenix and the cooler forested uplands toward Prescott and Payson, within a few hours' drive of the city. The landscape is rugged and dry, broken up by canyons and cliff lines. Granite is the most common rock, from the boulders and cliffs near Prescott to the slabs of the McDowell Mountains, while Queen Creek Canyon near Superior offers welded volcanic tuff with featured sport faces and pockets. Trad, bouldering and sport are all well represented, with most routes between 5.8 and 5.11 and boulder problems across the low and middle grades. Many crags work through most of the year: winter suits the lower desert, and shady or higher spots handle summer days.

co_boulder.blurb: Boulder lies where the Front Range meets the plains, and climbing starts almost at the edge of town. The Flatirons are tilted sandstone slabs on the skyline, offering trad, sport and bouldering. Eldorado Canyon, just south, has steep red conglomerate sandstone walls and is a major trad destination. Boulder Canyon to the west is mostly granite, with multi-pitch trad, sport and bouldering, while Flagstaff Mountain is the main local bouldering zone. Trad makes up the largest share, with sport and bouldering behind it. Grades cover everything, though most routes sit between 5.8 and 5.12, and boulder problems run from easy to very hard. Sunny weather and a large local climbing community keep the area busy.
